title: Equipment-resolution audit accepts unvalidated named-item candidates
description:
Found in PR #380 review (eshyra-erf5.3.3's srdEquipmentResolutionAudit.ts).

namedItemCandidates(key) in packages/core/src/rules/srdEquipmentResolutionAudit.ts
simply returns `[key]` without checking that `key` exists in the equipment
catalog. PROFICIENCY_PHRASE_RESOLVERS uses this helper for every named
single-item weapon/tool proficiency phrase (hand crossbows, Thieves' tools,
Herbalism kit, Daggers, etc.). assertEquipmentResolution() only checks
`candidateKeys.length > 0`, so a typo in one of these hard-coded keys (e.g.
`equipment:crossbow-hnad` instead of `equipment:crossbow-hand`) would still
pass the audit because it is a non-empty one-element array.

This weakens eshyra-erf5.3.3's claim: the audit proves broad filters
(weapon category/range, armor type, equipmentGroup) resolve against actual
equipment records, but for named single-item phrases it currently proves
only that a hard-coded string is non-empty, not that it exists in the
catalog.

Acceptance criteria:
- Either make namedItemCandidates() filter against the actual equipment
  catalog (only return the key if a record with that key/kind exists), or
  add a second assertion in assertEquipmentResolution() (or a dedicated
  check) that every returned candidateKey exists in the equipment catalog.
- Add a regression test where a named proficiency resolver points at a
  missing/misspelled equipment key and assert that resolution now fails
  (currently it would silently pass).

Likely files: packages/core/src/rules/srdEquipmentResolutionAudit.ts,
packages/core/test/srdEquipmentResolutionAudit.test.ts.
close_reason: namedItemCandidates() now validates keys against the equipment catalog; regression test added for a missing/misspelled named key. PR #381.
